title: AGENTS.md
text: package uses centralized color palette system stored inst/extdata/: - benvi_colors.rds: Named color definitions (e.g., “AzulQuinto”, “Floresta”, “Violeta”) - benvi_palette.rds: Pre-built palette collections inst/fonts/: Poppins font (4 weights: Regular, Bold, Italic, BoldItalic) bundled package. Registered automatically load systemfonts available. theme_benvi() defaults "Poppins" systemfonts ragg available, "sans" otherwise. runnable examples use base_family = "sans" \dontshow{options(theme_benvi.font_family = "sans")} CRAN compatibility. See dev/font-management.md details font management R packages. Palette Generation (data-raw/cols_to_palette.R): - Converts named colors hex values via get_colors() get_hex() functions - Creates palette sets organized type: - Theme palettes (4 colors): grays, browns, yellows, greens, blues, purples, pinks, oranges - Qualitative palettes (8 colors): qual_1 qual_9 - Sequential palettes (9 colors): seq_grays, seq_browns, seq_yellows, seq_greens, seq_blues, seq_purples, seq_pinks, seq_oranges - City-specific palettes: spo_seq, spo_div, spo_qual, rio_seq, rio_div, rio_qual, bhe_seq, bhe_div - Brand palettes: benvi_blue, benvi_purple, basic

title: AGENTS.md
text: R/benvi_palette.R: - benvi_palette(pal_name, n, direction, type): Main palette accessor - Returns hex colors named palettes - Supports discrete (exact colors) continuous (interpolated) modes - Can reverse palettes direction = -1 - pal_pal(): Internal factory function creating palette generators - print.palette(): S3 method visualizing palettes R/palette_utils.R: - show_palettes(type, n): Visual display palettes (like RColorBrewer::display.brewer.()). type one "", "theme", "sequential", "qualitative", "diverging", "city", "brand". R/benvi_scales.R: - Discrete scales: scale_color_benvi_d(), scale_fill_benvi_d() - Continuous scales: scale_color_benvi_c(), scale_fill_benvi_c() - use British/American spelling variants (color/colour) R/theme_benvi.R: - theme_benvi(): Exported custom ggplot2 theme; uses Poppins registered, falls back "sans". Override via options(theme_benvi.font_family = ...) base_family argument. R/fonts.R (font management): - font_status(): Reports Poppins ragg availability recommendations R/zzz.R: - .onLoad(): Auto-registers bundled Poppins font via systemfonts::register_font() systemfonts installed - register_bundled_poppins(): Internal — resolves font paths inst/fonts/ registers font R/save_plot.R: - ggsave_benvi(): Wrapper around ggplot2::ggsave() uses ragg device PNG available **R/plot_*.R** — wrapper functions (active): - plot_line(): Line chart - plot_column(): Column/bar chart (includes text labels, inside text via ggfittext) - plot_scatter(): Scatter plot optional regression line - plot_area(): Area chart - plot_histogram(): Histogram R/utils.R: - format_num_br(): Format numbers Brazilian locale (period thousands, comma decimal) R/utils-globals.R: Global variable bindings tidy eval (suppresses R CMD check notes) R/plot_scatter.R also contains: - plot_add_xy(): Internal — helper add axis lines plot

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benviplot provides color palettes ggplot2 helper functions exploratory data analysis. color schemes based Benvi, brand Brazilian proptech QuintoAndar1. package ships custom ggplot2 theme, family discrete continuous color scales, convenience wrappers common chart types.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
code: # Install remotes if needed install.packages("remotes")  remotes::install_github("viniciusoike/benviplot")

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benviplot bundles Poppins font family registers automatically package loads (requires systemfonts package). Poppins registered, theme_benvi() uses default. Without systemfonts, theme falls back system sans-serif font. best rendering quality custom fonts, install ragg package. ragg set graphics device (default RStudio Positron), Poppins renders correctly output formats. can check full font device status time :
code: install.packages("ragg") font_status()

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: core package theme_benvi() combined scale_*_benvi_*() functions. Together, give ggplot2 chart consistent look minimal effort. example , scale_fill_benvi_d() maps discrete cylinder variable "qual_8" qualitative palette, theme_benvi() handles rest styling.
code: library(ggplot2) library(benviplot) ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, fill = as.factor(cyl))) +   geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, color = "#000000") +   scale_fill_benvi_d(name = "Cylinders", pal_name = "qual_8") +   labs(     title = "Fuel Efficiency vs. Weight",     x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",     y = "Miles per Gallon"   ) +   theme_benvi()

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: package organizes palettes several families: theme, sequential, qualitative, diverging, city-specific, brand. family serves different purpose, choosing right one depends nature variable.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: show_palettes() gives visual overview available palettes. Calling without arguments displays every palette package; pass type name narrow output. can filter type: "theme", "sequential", "qualitative", "city", "brand".
code: show_palettes() show_palettes("sequential")

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benvi_palette() returns named vector hex codes. Printing renders color swatch console, useful quick visual comparison. use colors outside ggplot2 (e.g. base R input another package), coerce plain character vector. Discrete palettes contain 4 9 fixed colors. need granularity, set type = "continuous" interpolate arbitrary number colors along palette gradient.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: scale functions follow standard ggplot2 naming convention: scale_{aesthetic}_benvi_{d|c}(), d discrete variables c continuous ones. color fill variants available, colour spellings work expected.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: Discrete scales map categorical variables qualitative city-specific palette. pal_name argument (first positional argument) selects palette use.
code: iqaiw_total <- subset(iqaiw, rooms == "Total")  ggplot(iqaiw_total, aes(x = date, y = index, color = name_muni)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 100) +   scale_color_benvi_d("rio_qual", name = NULL) +   labs(     title = "IQAIW Rental Index by City",     x = NULL,     y = "Index (base = 100)"   ) +   theme_benvi()

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: Continuous scales interpolate across sequential brand palette. well suited heatmaps, choropleths, visualization numeric variable needs smooth color gradient. Use direction = -1 reverse palette.
code: iqaiw_total <- subset(iqaiw_total, !is.na(acum12m))  ggplot(iqaiw_total, aes(x = date, y = name_muni, fill = acum12m * 100)) +   geom_tile(height = 0.6, color = "#ffffff") +   scale_fill_benvi_c(     pal_name = "benvi_blue",     name = "YoY Change (%)",     direction = -1   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = seq(2023, 2025, 1),     expand = expansion(0)   ) +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +   theme_benvi() +   theme(     legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.75),     axis.text = element_text(size = 12),     panel.grid = element_blank()   )

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benviplot includes convenience wrappers common chart types. functions accept data frame column names via tidy evaluation, apply theme_benvi() automatically, return standard ggplot2 object. designed quick exploratory work; publication-quality figures, building plot scratch gives full control.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_line() draws single-series line chart. Pass color map grouping variable get multiple lines automatic legend.
code: plot_line(economics, x = date, y = uempmed)

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_column() creates vertical bar chart. Setting text = TRUE adds value labels bar; bars enough height, text_inside = TRUE places labels inside bars instead (requires ggfittext package).
code: sales <- data.frame(   cities = c(     "São Paulo",     "Rio de Janeiro",     "Belo Horizonte",     "Porto Alegre",     "Curitiba"   ),   revenue = c(125, 200, 150, 175, 80) )  plot_column(sales, x = cities, y = revenue, text = TRUE)

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_scatter() maps x y scatter plot. color argument maps grouping variable point fill using Benvi palette. Set smooth = TRUE overlay regression line.
code: plot_scatter(   mtcars,   x = wt,   y = mpg,   color = as.factor(cyl),   palette = "qual_5",   scale_name = "Cylinders" )

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: helpers return ggplot2 objects, can extend additional layers, scales, theme adjustments normally .
code: plot_line(economics, x = date, y = unemploy / 1000) +   geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = benvi_palette("oranges")[3]) +   labs(     title = "US Unemployment with Smoothed Trend",     subtitle = "Unemployment figures in millions",     x = NULL,     y = "Unemployed (millions)",     caption = "Data: economics dataset"   )

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: palettes tied ggplot2. Since benvi_palette() returns plain hex codes, can use anywhere accepts color strings, including base R graphics, lattice, plotting system.
code: colors <- as.character(benvi_palette("purples"))  plot(   mtcars$wt,   mtcars$mpg,   col = colors[mtcars$cyl / 2 - 1],   pch = 19,   cex = 1.5,   xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",   ylab = "Miles per Gallon",   main = "Using Benvi colors in base R" )

code: # Rental price index for major cities index_data <- iqaiw |>   filter(     rooms %in% c("1", "2"),     between(date, as.Date("2023-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-31"))   )  ggplot(index_data, aes(date, index, color = rooms)) +   geom_line(lwd = 0.7) +   facet_wrap(vars(name_muni)) +   scale_color_benvi_d() +   labs(     title = "IQAIW Rental Index by City",     x = NULL,     y = "Index (base = 100)",     color = "Rooms",     caption = "Source: IQAIW (benviplot)"   ) +   theme_benvi() # Price per m2 by city over time index_data <- iqaiw |>   filter(     rooms == "Total",     between(date, as.Date("2023-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-31"))   ) |>   mutate(xdate = lubridate::year(date) + (lubridate::month(date) - 1) / 12)  ggplot(index_data, aes(x = xdate, y = name_muni, fill = acum12m * 100)) +   geom_tile(height = 0.6, color = "gray90") +   scale_fill_benvi_c(     pal_name = "benvi_blue",     name = "YoY Change (%)",     direction = -1   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = seq(2023, 2025, 1),     expand = expansion(0)   ) +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +   theme_benvi() +   theme(     legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.75),     axis.text = element_text(size = 12),     panel.grid = element_blank()   ) sales <- data.frame(   x = factor(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)),   y = c(200, 220, 230, 210, 240, 290) )  plot_column(sales, x = x, y = y, text = TRUE)

title: Plot a histogram chart — plot_histogram
text: method parameter controls algorithm used compute optimal bin width. Available methods: "fd" "FD" Freedman-Diaconis rule (default). Robust outliers, uses IQR. Formula: \(2 * IQR / n^{1/3}\). Best distributions. "Scott" Scott's rule. Uses standard deviation. Formula: \(3 * sd / n^{1/3}\). Works well normal-like distributions. "Sturges" Sturges' formula. Simple logarithmic rule. Formula: \(k = \lceil log_2(n) \rceil\) bins. Good roughly normal data. "Rice" Rice rule. Cube root based. Formula: \(k = \lceil 2n^{1/3} \rceil\) bins. General purpose rule. "sqrt" Square root rule. Formula: \(k = \lceil \sqrt{n} \rceil\) bins. Simple, tends oversmooth. doubt, use default "fd" (Freedman-Diaconis), robust works well across different distributions.

title: benviplot 1.1.2
text: plot_column() gains three new parameters: text_inside (renders labels inside bars via ggfittext), text_place, text_padding. plot_column_label() deprecated. Use plot_column(text_inside = TRUE) instead. plot_line_trend() deprecated. Use geom_smooth() manual trend lines instead.
